local_checks.result: aws_cli_release_version reads https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/version.txt with the bounded curl, strips whitespace, and refuses anything but ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ (install/common/aws_cli.sh:29-38). The value can therefore name a URL path segment (awscli-exe-linux-<arch>-<version>.zip, :61) and an install.sh --version argument (:175-176) and nothing else. The archive or install.sh and its .sig are verified against the pinned key fingerprint (:20) by the verification steps U311 does not change (:146-172). On Linux the CLI unzipped from the archive must report exactly the requested release before the upstream installer runs (:181-188). main skips only when the installed CLI already runs as that release, the same predicate as the postcondition. The ETag state file is retired and removed by home/.chezmoiremove:22. No secret is involved, and the version string reaches no eval.

hardening_notes: version.txt is unsigned and the kit holds no minimum version. Whoever can answer that HTTPS request (a TLS interception the host trusts, or AWS's origin) can name an older release that is still signed, and the kit installs it. The unversioned latest pair it replaced had the same exposure. A floor in the manifest (refuse a release older than the installed one, or older than a pinned minimum) would make a downgrade a refusal.
